page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY processor cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the CPU includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.hfc6.2xlarge consistently in the average tier across most compute and memory workloads. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1244.0 and a multi-core score of 4795.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 8939.31. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only cached small block speeds of 426.41 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds of 49.31 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the CPU's support for AVX-512 vector instructions assists in cryptography and compression, yielding a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 24.96 GB/sec and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 37.32 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits a clear performance tradeoff when handling larger computational models. While small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model runs efficiently at 130.25 tokens/sec for text generation, scaling up to a medium 7B model results in poor prompt processing at 11.39 tokens/sec and weak text generation at 6.44 tokens/sec due to the lack of GPU acceleration and limited memory capacity. Consequently, this instance is best suited for compute-intensive workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage, such as static web serving, Redis database operations, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing.
